entries.sentence: Lung cancer is mostly divided into two groups, called non-small cell and small cell lung cancer.
entries.note: Search summary: mostly split into non-small cell and small cell; blended from Roy Castle types page and Christie page

entries.sentence: Roy Castle says around 85 in every 100 people with lung cancer have a non-small cell type and about 15 in 100 have small cell lung cancer.
entries.note: Returned text gave about 85% non-small cell and about 15% small cell

entries.sentence: Adenocarcinoma is the most common kind of non-small cell cancer. It grows more slowly than some other types, but it can spread early.
entries.note: Summary: most common non-small cell subtype, slower growing, can spread early

entries.sentence: Squamous cell carcinoma starts in the cells that line the airways and is often caused by smoking.
entries.note: Summary: develops in cells lining the airways, often caused by smoking

entries.sentence: Large cell carcinoma is less common and tends to spread outside the lung at an earlier stage than other non-small cell types.
entries.note: Summary: less common, more aggressive, spreads outside lung earlier

entries.sentence: Small cell lung cancer grows and spreads more quickly than the non-small cell types and is strongly linked with smoking.
entries.note: Summary: grows and spreads more quickly; one source notes strong smoking link

entries.sentence: Because small cell cancer often spreads quite early, doctors generally treat it as if it has spread, whether or not a secondary cancer shows up.
entries.note: Summary statement; page not identified, blended

entries.sentence: Knowing the type matters, because the NHS says treatment depends on the type of lung cancer and how far it has spread.
entries.note: NHS treatment page summary: depends on type and how far it has spread

entries.sentence: Staging describes how far a cancer has grown and spread. Cancer Research UK says the TNM system is the most common way to stage lung cancer.
entries.note: Returned text: TNM most common way to stage lung cancer. First clause (what staging describes) is a plain textbook explanation, not quoted

entries.sentence: The number system uses TNM to place lung cancers into stages 1 to 4.
entries.note: Returned text: number staging systems use TNM; four stages for lung cancer numbered 1 to 4

entries.sentence: Macmillan says doctors use the same staging system for non-small cell and small cell lung cancer.
entries.note: Returned text from Macmillan staging page

entries.sentence: Small cell lung cancer may also be described as limited or extensive stage. Cancer Research UK calls this an older, simpler system that is becoming less common.
entries.note: Returned text: older and simpler system, use declining

entries.sentence: Limited stage means the cancer is within a single area on one side of the chest. Extensive stage means it has spread beyond a single area that can be treated with radiotherapy.
entries.note: Returned text: limited = single area one side of chest; extensive = beyond a single radiotherapy area

entries.sentence: Cancer Research UK adds that extensive disease generally means stage 4 small cell lung cancer.
entries.note: Returned text: generally means a stage 4 small cell lung cancer

entries.sentence: Roy Castle says stage 4 lung cancer is not curable but it is treatable, and many people can live well with advanced cancer.
entries.note: Returned text: stage 4 is not curable, it is treatable, and many people can live well with advanced cancer

entries.sentence: A chest X-ray is often one of the first tests when a GP has any concern about lung cancer.
entries.note: Returned text: if GP has concerns, one of the first tests may be a chest x-ray

entries.sentence: A CT scan is the main imaging step. It helps show where the cancer is and whether it may have spread to other organs, and the person lies on a table that slides into the scanner.
entries.note: Summary of CT step; Cancer Research UK / Roy Castle test pages, blended

entries.sentence: In a bronchoscopy, a thin scope is passed through the airways so doctors can look inside and take a tiny tissue sample, called a biopsy.
entries.note: Returned text on bronchoscopy; blended

entries.sentence: Sometimes a needle biopsy through the skin is used instead. The radiologist asks the person to hold their breath while a fine needle goes through the skin into the lung.
entries.note: Returned text from needle biopsy page

entries.sentence: Pressure may be felt during sampling, and a chest X-ray usually follows an hour or more later to check the lung.
entries.note: Returned text: pressure may be felt; chest X-ray an hour or more later. 'to check the lung' is an inference, not stated

entries.sentence: Other tests can include a PET-CT scan, a blood test for tumour DNA and a bone scan to check whether the cancer has spread.
entries.note: Summary: other tests PET-CT, liquid biopsy, bone scan; blended

entries.sentence: The NHS says surgery is the main option for lung cancer, and that chemotherapy, radiotherapy, targeted medicines or immunotherapy may also be used.
entries.note: NHS treatment page summary

entries.sentence: Cancer Research UK says surgery is generally for early-stage disease, and after surgery the doctor may offer treatment to lower the chance of the cancer coming back.
entries.note: Summary attributed to Cancer Research UK non-small cell treatment page

entries.sentence: Radiotherapy is often used on its own, but it may also be given together with or after chemotherapy or surgery.
entries.note: Leeds Teaching Hospitals page text

entries.sentence: Small cell lung cancer is usually treated with chemotherapy, on its own or with radiotherapy.
entries.note: NHS 111 Wales text

entries.sentence: Targeted drugs are used when a tumour has a specific genetic change, so tumour samples are sent for genetic testing to look for targets.
entries.note: 111 Wales: targeted therapy; St George's: samples sent to genomics hub for sequencing to identify targets; blended

entries.sentence: NHS 111 Wales notes that targeted therapies cannot cure lung cancer but can slow its spread.
entries.note: Returned text from NHS 111 Wales

entries.sentence: The NHS says targeted medicines or immunotherapy are sometimes used for advanced lung cancer that has spread to other parts of the body.
entries.note: NHS treatment page summary

entries.sentence: Roy Castle says courses of immunotherapy often have a time limit, as long as the cancer keeps responding and there are no troublesome side effects.
entries.note: Summary of Roy Castle text on immunotherapy courses; exact page uncertain (stage 4 page returned in same search). Number of months deliberately omitted

entries.sentence: Cancer Research UK says tiredness can come on during treatment, tends to get worse as treatment goes on, and can last for some weeks afterwards. Resting while also doing some gentle physical activity can help.
entries.note: Returned text on tiredness; page not individually confirmed (summary of radiotherapy/chemoradiotherapy side-effect pages)

entries.sentence: Chest radiotherapy can cause a dry cough or breathlessness soon after treatment. Scarring can develop later, and steroids or other medicines can help with breathing.
entries.note: Returned text: dry cough or shortness of breath soon after; scarring later; steroids/other medicines help

entries.sentence: Clinical nurse specialists give information and support during treatment. Palliative care nurses help with symptoms such as pain and sickness, and also support carers.
entries.note: Summary: clinical nurse specialists, community palliative care nurses give symptom control and emotional support; page not identified

entries.sentence: A GP can usually arrange for a specialist nurse to visit at home.
entries.note: Returned text: GP can usually arrange to be seen by specialist nurse at home

entries.sentence: Cancer Research UK suggests that sharing worries can make them seem less overwhelming, and that many people find counselling helpful.
entries.note: Returned text from coping page

entries.sentence: After treatment, the first check-up is usually within 4 to 6 weeks, with later visits spaced further apart and including blood tests, X-rays and scans.
entries.note: Returned text from Cancer Research UK follow-up page

entries.sentence: Non-small cell lung cancer is the larger group, with adenocarcinoma, squamous cell and large cell types.
entries.note: Summary subtypes
